subtopics.title: Closed, Open, and the Four Participants

questions.question: South Africa is described as an OPEN economy because:
options: It trades with the foreign sector — exporting platinum, citrus and vehicles and importing oil and machinery

questions.question: In the four-sector model, BUSINESSES are the participant that:
options: Owns the factors of production and pays tax on wages
Hires factor services, produces goods and services, pays out incomes and invests in capital goods
Collects taxes and supplies public goods

questions.question: Rands are swapped for dollars, euros and yuan in the:
The difference between the REAL flow and the MONEY flow is that:
options: The real flow is measured yearly and the money flow monthly
The money flow only involves government
The real flow exists only in a closed economy
The real flow carries factor services and goods one way, while the money flow carries incomes and expenditure the opposite way

subtopics.title: Leakages, Injections and the Equilibrium Condition

questions.question: Which list pairs each leakage with the injection that shares its door?
options: Saving with investment (financial market), taxation with government spending, imports with exports
Saving with exports, taxation with investment, imports with government spending
Consumption with saving, tax with imports, exports with investment
Wages with profit, rent with interest, tax with subsidies

questions.question: The open-economy equilibrium condition states that:
options: S = I, T = G and M = X must each hold separately
Total leakages equal total injections: S + T + M = I + G + X

questions.question: S = R250bn, T = R550bn, M = R300bn; I = R300bn, G = R500bn, X = R300bn. The economy is:
options: Contracting, because saving is below investment
Expanding, because tax exceeds government spending
In equilibrium — leakages of R1 100bn equal injections of R1 100bn

questions.question: In that data set, T exceeds G by R50bn while I exceeds S by R50bn. This shows that:
options: The economy must be in disequilibrium
Individual pairs need not match — only the TOTALS of leakages and injections must be equal

subtopics.title: Measuring the Flow — Three Methods, Three Aggregates

questions.question: The production method sums value ADDED rather than turnover so that:
options: The flour inside the bread is not counted at the mill and again at the bakery

questions.question: GDP at market prices is R7 000bn, taxes on products R800bn, subsidies on products R120bn. GDP at factor cost is:
With GDP of R7 000bn, primary income received from abroad of R90bn and primary income paid abroad of R260bn, GNI equals:
Nominal GDP is R7 000bn and the deflator is 125 on a base of 100. Real GDP is:
options: R5 600bn — and only real growth means more actual goods

questions.question: When exports fall so that leakages exceed injections, the adjustment sequence is:
options: Stock accumulates → production cut → retrenchments → incomes fall → S, T and M shrink → equilibrium at a LOWER national income
Prices rise → wages rise → output rises
The rand strengthens → imports fall → equilibrium is unchanged
Government spending falls automatically to match

questions.question: An injection into an economy ALREADY at full capacity produces mainly:
options: Inflation — the extra spending cannot summon extra goods

questions.question: "Self-correcting in direction but not in outcome" warns that:
options: Equilibrium can never return after a shock
Prices always return to their starting level
The flow always finds a new balance, but that balance may include mass unemployment — balance is not the same as well-being
Policy can never change the equilibrium

questions.question: Match the instruments: fiscal policy, monetary policy and trade policy respectively move:
options: X and M; G and T; S and I
S and I; X and M; G and T
G and T; S and I through the interest rate; X and M

subtopics.title: The Money That Goes Around the Township

questions.question: The seamstress supplies work and the factory returns money; she returns the money as spending and receives goods. The two rings are:
options: One carrying things and one carrying rands, turning in opposite directions

questions.question: A salary spent at the corner shop becoming part of somebody else's pay next month-end shows that money:
options: Circulates — spending returns to businesses and re-emerges as income
Loses value each time it changes hands

questions.question: In the month-end story, the FOREIGN sector appears as:
options: The clinic sister and the pothole team
Imported fabric arriving by container and jeans exported to Europe

questions.question: In the water-tank picture, the LEVEL of the water stands for:
options: National income — the size of the economy

questions.question: The three DRAINS carrying money out of the flow are:
The tank's level holds steady when:
options: Every tap matches its own drain exactly
The taps TOGETHER match the drains TOGETHER — R1 100bn in against R1 100bn out in our figures

questions.question: "One tank, three dipsticks" refers to:
options: Nominal, real and per capita GDP
The production, income and expenditure methods, which must report the same total

subtopics.title: When the Bucket Won't Sit Still

questions.question: Europe cuts its jeans orders and export earnings fall from R300bn to R240bn. The first thing the factory notices is:
options: Finished stock piling up in the storeroom, leading it to drop a shift

questions.question: The level settles again at a LOWER point because falling incomes mean:
options: Government closes the drains by law
Less is saved, less tax is paid and fewer imports are bought — the drains narrow until they match the weakened taps

questions.question: If the factory is already running every machine around the clock, an extra injection mainly produces:
options: Higher PRICES — spending rises but output cannot

questions.question: In tap-and-drain language, a weaker rand that makes exports cheaper for foreign buyers is:
options: A wider EXPORT tap — an injection into the flow
